title: microbatch-sm-saturation-lab-notes-oct-2025
content:
Purpose and context:
Quick lab notes from a focused profiling run to understand why micro-batching (batch sizes 1..8) is showing poor SM saturation and elevated token p99 for short sequences (seq_len 8-32). Goal: identify dominant kernel bottlenecks, quantify achieved occupancy vs theoretical, and test whether CUDA Graph capture materially reduces launch overhead for small batches.

Setup (hardware/software):
- GPU: A100-SXM4 80GB, CUDA 12.1, driver 535.xx
- Runtime: internal-serving v0.37.1 (w/ continuous-batching enabled, default cache warmup disabled)
- Models: opt-6.7b float16 baseline and quantized int8 variant with fused attention kernels (local branch q8-fused)
- Workloads: interactive microbatch workloads: (batch, seq_in, seq_gen) triplets tested: (1,8,8), (2,16,8), (4,32,16), (8,32,8)
- Tools: Nsight Systems 2025.3 for timeline traces, Nsight Compute 2025.1 for per-kernel metrics, cuLaunchActivity sampling off, CUDA Graph capture via runtime API test harness

Command snippets used:
- nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=run_B2_S16 run_inference.sh --batch 2 --seq 16
- ncu --metrics achieved_occupancy,sm_efficiency,sm_activity,dram_read_throughput,inst_issued_per_warp --target-processes all --set full run_inference.sh --batch 2

Key observations (summary):
1) Low achieved occupancy on attention kernels for small batches: Nsight Compute reports achieved_occupancy ~0.37 (37%) for attention forward CUDA kernel (attn_fwd_v2) at batch=1 seq=8. The theoretical occupancy bound for this kernel on A100 is ~0.72 given block/grid config.
2) Kernel launch overhead and scheduling gaps dominate timeline at microbatch sizes: Nsight Systems CPU/GPU timeline shows frequent 100-300us gaps between launches when batch<=2. These gaps correlate with host-side enqueue / dynamic parameterization work (lock contention in batching coordinator).
3) Persistent-kernel-friendly stages (token generation loops) show higher SM efficiency: the fused-ffn kernel (ffn_fused_relu_gelu) achieves sm_efficiency ~0.81 and higher sustained occupancy for larger workloads (batch>=4).
4) CUDA Graph capture reduced CPU-side gaps significantly: for batch=2 seq=16, capture reduced inter-kernel idle time by ~65%, improved p95 latency by ~18% and increased achieved_occupancy of lightweight kernels from 0.37->0.52. However, capture requires careful handling of KV cache pointer variability which forced one-time memcpy during capture and added complexity for caching layer.
5) Memory-bound kernels show DRAM throughput underutilized: some miscellaneous kernel (kv_update_shard) had dram_read_throughput at ~45% of peak for A100 which suggests either non-coalesced accesses or small working set per warp for microbatches.
6) Launch configuration mismatch: many kernels were launched with small block sizes (64-128 threads/block) leading to low warps per SM occupancy. Increasing block size to 256/512 in a synthetic test increased achieved_occupancy by ~15-20% but required tuning of shared memory footprint.

Detailed notes and evidence:
- Nsight Systems timeline (B1_S8): repeated pattern: host serializes per-request NVTX regions -> kernel1(attn_fwd) -> 120us idle -> kernel2(ffn) -> 160us idle -> kernel3(kv_update). The idle slots are where scheduling and parameter setup occurs.
- NCU per-kernel for attn_fwd_v2 (batch=1 seq=8): achieved_occupancy 0.37, sm_efficiency 48%, ipc 0.72, top stalls: warp_execution_stall (40%), instr_issue_stall (28%).
- After enabling a micro-batching coalescer (local branch coalesce-15): observed reduction in host-side queuing work and lower inter-kernel idle time, but added latency for first token in a request. Tradeoff acceptable for throughput-oriented endpoints, not for strict latency p50 SLAs.

Hypotheses and root causes prioritized:
A) Host-side batching coordination cost is a first-order contributor to gaps at small batch sizes. Solution direction: move more serialization into device via persistent kernels or preallocated CUDA Graphs.
B) Kernel launch configuration is conservative; kernels are using small block sizes for historic portability assumptions, hurting SM occupancy on modern GPUs. Solution direction: parameterize kernel launch by hardware detection and tune thread/block and shared memory usage per model shape.
C) Some kernels are memory-bound due to uncoalesced access patterns when microbatching with per-item offsets. Solution direction: rework data layout to contiguous per-thread-chunk memory and pad to 128B alignment where necessary.

Quick experiments run (and results):
- Experiment 1: CUDA Graph capture for token loop (batch=2 seq=16): p95 latency down 18%, achieved_occupancy of attn_fwd + small kernels up 0.37->0.52. Caveats: graph capture cost on first call ~2-3ms and invalidation when KV cache pointers change.
- Experiment 2: Block size increase (attn kernels): synthetic compile with 256 threads/block -> achieved_occupancy +17% but observed 5% increase in register spilling for ffn kernels; need to balance registers vs threads.
- Experiment 3: Persistent kernel prototype (single long-running kernel that services a small request queue on device): removed host enqueue gaps entirely in microbench, p99 reduced by ~28% in controlled lab. Integration complexity high (synchronization with host, fallbacks).

Actionable recommendations (short-term):
1) Prototype device-side CUDA Graph approach for the token generation hot path and measure in 1% traffic bucket. Add guard rails for KV-pointer variability (use stable scratch pointers during capture).
2) Add an autotuning path to set kernel block size and shared-memory knobs at model load time (store tuned configs per model-sequence-shape). Start with opt-6.7b and run for seq_len bins [8,16,32,64].
3) Optimize host batching coordinator: reduce lock hold time, move serialization to a pre-flight stage that can be parallelized, instrument NVTX around coordinator to reduce 100-300us gaps.
4) Revisit memory layout for kv_update_shard and attention input packing to ensure coalesced loads for microbatch code paths; add microbench for dram throughput.

Longer-term directions (research/engineering):
- Invest in persistent kernels for latency-sensitive tiny batches; explore hybrid approach where persistent kernel handles batches <=2 and normal kernel path used otherwise.
- Consider a small-device-side queue abstraction that exposes a low-latency submit API to reduce host roundtrips.
- Expand autotuner to include quantized kernels (int8) and fused kernels to capture combined effects on register pressure and occupancy.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How stable are CUDA Graph benefits across different driver versions and MIG partitions? Need further cross-GPU validation.
- Does persistent kernel regain benefits when under contention from multi-tenant workloads (Dedicated pools)? We should test with 2-3 concurrent tenants.
- Are there any security/observability drawbacks to moving more logic to device? Need SRE and security signoff.

Next steps and owners:
- Aisha: prototype CUDA Graph capture harness and report metrics back (INF-2147) — due 2025-10-20.
- Mateo: implement simple block-size autotune in dev branch, collect NCU/throughput tradeoffs for opt-6.7b — due 2025-10-24.
- Liu: measure memory access pattern changes for kv_update_shard and propose layout patch — due 2025-10-21.
- Rita: run cross-driver validation on T4 and A100 (driver matrix) and test graph capture invalidation cases — due 2025-10-27.

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Keep logs of the first-call capture overhead for CUDA Graph; might need an async warmup path for 0-latency-critical requests.
- Consider adding a per-model "microbatch-optimized" flag that flips to persistent kernel/graph path behind the scenes.

Appendix: quick paste of a representative NCU snippet (attn_fwd_v2, batch=1 seq=8):
- achieved_occupancy: 0.37
- sm_efficiency: 48%
- dram_read_throughput: 38% peak
- top stall reasons: warp_execution_stall, instr_issue_stall

End of notes.
